parsed.rationale: The candidate implementation matches the governing unit's maximum interval of 35 calendar days for evaluating security patches.
The candidate implementation's 21-day cadence is stricter (more frequent) than the governing unit's maximum 35-day interval, thus satisfying the requirement.
The candidate implementation's quarterly (90-day) evaluation cadence exceeds the governing unit's maximum interval of 35 calendar days, failing to meet the required frequency.

The implementation reviews weekly (every 7 days), satisfying the maximum interval of 15 days, but it does not explicitly address reviewing a summarization or sampling of all logged events as required.
The candidate implementation lacks a mandated review interval of no greater than 15 calendar days, contradicting the governing unit's requirement.
The candidate implementation is null, indicating no implementation addresses the governing unit.
The candidate implementation enforces training at most every 12 months, which is stricter (shorter interval) than the governing maximum of 15 months, thus satisfying the requirement.
The implementation grants access before training completion, violating the governing unit's requirement that training be completed prior to granting access.
The packet is marked incomplete and lacks the definition of 'CIP Exceptional Circumstances', which is required to assess compliance.

The candidate implementation exercises the OT recovery plan annually via a tabletop scenario, which satisfies the governing unit's requirement to test at least once every 15 calendar months using an allowed method (paper drill or tabletop exercise).

The candidate implementation only mentions review of the recovery plan upon infrastructure changes and does not satisfy the mandatory testing requirement of at least once every 15 calendar months using specified methods.
The candidate implementation specifies a 1-year update deadline, which exceeds the governing unit's maximum of 180 days, thus contradicting the requirement.
The candidate implementation's 10 business day deadline is stricter than the governing unit's 30 calendar day maximum, thus satisfying the requirement.
The candidate implementation monitors every 24 hours, which is more frequent than the maximum 35-day interval required, thus satisfying the monitoring obligation.

The candidate implementation's semi-annual (approximately every 182-184 days) monitoring interval exceeds the governing unit's maximum interval of 35 calendar days, thus failing to satisfy the required monitoring frequency.
The annual active vulnerability assessment meets the maximum 15-month cadence requirement specified in the governing unit.

The candidate implementation references CIP-003-8, which does not contain the required vendor electronic remote access security controls, contradicting the governing unit's requirement from CIP-003-9.
The candidate references a non-existent requirement (CIP-010-2 R1.5), making the mapping unclear and necessitating abstention due to missing premise.

The candidate implementation satisfies the governing unit by having the locally defined 'Critical Infrastructure Protection Officer' (aligned to the NERC Glossary term 'CIP Senior Manager') approve the identification list at least once every 15 calendar months.
The candidate implementation is null, indicating no implementation addresses the governing unit.
The candidate implementation delays alerting until the next business day, which exceeds the 15-minute maximum specified in the governing unit.
The candidate implementation addresses only authorized electronic access, omitting the required training prior to authorized unescorted physical access to applicable Cyber Assets.
The candidate implementation reviews the identification inventory every 12 months, which is more frequent than the governing unit's maximum of 15 months, thus satisfying the requirement.
The packet is incomplete because it does not state whether the entity has any Dial-up Connectivity, which is required to assess satisfaction of the conditional obligation.
The candidate implementation enforces a password change interval of 24 months, which exceeds the governing unit's maximum interval of 15 calendar months, directly contradicting the requirement.

The candidate implementation enforces a maximum password age of 365 days (approximately 1 year), which is shorter than the governing unit's maximum of 15 calendar months (approximately 1.25 years), thus contradicting the specified maximum interval.
The candidate implementation describes reactive monitoring of vendor bulletins without an explicit, scheduled vulnerability assessment occurring at least once every 15 months as required.
The candidate implementation excerpt is truncated, lacking the cadence clause required to assess compliance with the governing unit.

The candidate implementation only requires training at onboarding and makes refresher training optional, failing to meet the governing unit's mandate for training at least once every 15 calendar months.
The packet is incomplete, lacking candidate text for elements 4.1, 4.3, and 4.4 required by the ALL_OF condition.
